clue.text: Game *played by leader in forward position

parts.note: bridge is a card game
a head is a leader, as of a school or department

explanation.surface: A card game is played by whoever has taken the lead from an advanced post.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a secured foothold pushed out into enemy territory, the most advanced military position.

clue.text: Old dandies making money in America.

explanation.surface: Old dandies made a fortune in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Regency fops and dashing young men were called bucks; in the US a buck is a dollar.

clue.text: Offhand union leader upholding claim to punctuality

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece holding up another sits below it, so it comes after

parts.note: someone claiming punctuality says I'm prompt

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A casual trade union boss backs a boast about being on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upholding' puts U underneath in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Offhand here means spoken without preparation, unrehearsed and spontaneous.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-well obtains a lot of merchandise gratis

indicators.note: a lot of something is most of it but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: goods are merchandise
gratis means free, for nothing

explanation.surface: A layabout gets hold of much stock without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last letter of GOODS, leaving GOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A ne'er-do-well is a lazy, worthless person, the same as a wastrel or layabout.

clue.text: Like a spearhead formed by an army at the double?

indicators.note: the word for speed is formed with the army placed in its middle

parts.note: at the double means quickly, with haste
TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An arrowhead formation adopted by troops on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed by' is the insertion signal: the speed word is built around the army. TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastate, from Latin hasta for spear, describes a leaf or point shaped like a spear's tip.

clue.text: Harsh as the -south wind before the end of June

indicators.note: one piece comes before the other in the answer

parts.note: Auster is the Latin name for the south wind

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Weather as severe as a southerly gale before the end of June.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe, stern and harsh.

clue.text: Reel in float

explanation.surface: An angler's reel bobs in the water beside the float.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to feel dizzy, as when the head spins; and to float in water is to be buoyed up, as a body drifting in a pool.

clue.text: Sound method to calculate load

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is heard rather than read as written

parts.note: a way is a method

explanation.surface: A reliable technique for working out a cargo's weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh is to find out how heavy something is, measuring its burden.

clue.text: Old soldier encountered always around a river

indicators.note: the word for met goes around the river name

parts.note: encountered means met
the Usk is a river in Wales
e'er is the poetic shortening of ever, always

explanation.surface: A veteran was always meeting others by the riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: A musketeer was a soldier armed with a musket, a type from centuries past.

clue.text: Spiritual type, but he has us all. taped!

definitions.text: Spiritual type, but he has us all. taped!

parts.words: Spiritual type, but he has us all. taped!
parts.note: a heavenly being is pictured as making a record, like a tape, of every human deed; 'taped' reads like 'sized up'

explanation.surface: A religious man who has everyone figured out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has us all taped' sounds like slang for knowing our tricks, but it means our deeds are all written down.
explanation.definitionFit: In tradition, an angel keeps a ledger of each person's good and bad acts for the Last Judgement.

clue.text: Senior officer, devout and profuse in speech

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer
devout means pious

explanation.surface: A commander who is religious and talks at great length.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means abundant or plentiful; of a speaker or writer, it means wordy and expansive.

clue.text: The kind that's found in glasses

indicators.note: something found in another lies inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles, glasses
that is, in Latin id est, is abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A description of the sort of drink served in a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' expands to 'that is', the i.e. abbreviation, rather than acting as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or sort, as in a particular type of animal or plant.

clue.text: Bit of a downfall for student in drug swindle?.

parts.note: snow is slang for cocaine

indicators.note: the student goes in, placed inside the word for the swindle

parts.note: a fake is a fraud or swindle
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A student ruined by a narcotics scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downfall' looks like ruin, but here it means falling snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A single crystal of falling snow is one small piece of a snowfall.

clue.text: Scottish loch reputed to 'contain native pigment

indicators.note: the words loch reputed contain the run of letters across their join

explanation.surface: A lake in Scotland is said to hold a local colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a natural earth pigment, yellow to brown, occurring in the ground as a mineral.

clue.text: He manages to deal in horses

explanation.surface: A man who gets by trading horses.
explanation.definitionFit: One who copes is someone who manages; and a coper is also an old word for a horse dealer, from an old verb meaning to barter.

clue.text: Maeterlinck, for one, said to be such a player

indicators.note: said to be tells us the word for the writer's school is spoken

parts.note: Maurice Maeterlinck, Belgian playwright, belonged to the Symbolist movement

explanation.surface: The Belgian playwright supposedly played in the percussion section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such a player' depends on the sound-alike: the player is a percussionist.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussionist who plays the clashing brass discs in an orchestra.

clue.text: English chaps "play half heartedly, but can be made to improve

parts.note: chaps are men

indicators.note: with half its heart gone, the word loses one of the two letters at its centre

parts.note: to dabble is to play at something without commitment

explanation.surface: English men play without commitment but can be pushed to get better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half heartedly' takes one of the two Bs from the middle of DABBLE, leaving DABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct or improve a text, so something emendable is open to correction.

clue.text: Society girl upset 22, an ally in retirement

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: deb is short for debutante, a young woman entering high society
22 down's answer is a teacher, and a university teacher is a fellow

explanation.surface: A debutante, upset, finds the teacher a companion in old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' looks like old age but means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedfellow is an associate or partner, literally someone who shares your bed when you turn in.

clue.text: Quiet about gold only found in a tomb

indicators.note: one word goes about, or around, the others

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keep mum
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
sole means only

explanation.surface: Silence surrounds gold found only in a burial place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' goes with 'Quiet', which wraps around both the gold and the 'only' words, not just the one next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mausoleum is a grand building housing a tomb or tombs.

clue.text: He takes in workers, and can hide the proceeds

indicators.note: proceeds, things made by working material over, signals the letters are worked into something new

explanation.surface: A man who employs staff and can conceal the profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' are ants, eaten by this spiny anteater; 'proceeds' turns 'can hide' into a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny anteater of Australia feeds on ants and termites, the insect world's labourers.

clue.text: Spring, examination concerning the council chairman

parts.note: May is a month of spring
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: In spring an exam about the head of the local council.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayoral means relating to a mayor, the chair of a town council.

clue.text: Free article rejected in the pits

indicators.note: rejected is taken as sent back, so the whole sequence of letters is read backwards

parts.note: to rid is to free
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article given away for nothing is turned down in the mines.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point; 'the pits' is slang for the worst there is.

clue.text: A minor irritation. for 23's leading character

parts.note: an itch is a small irritation

explanation.surface: A small annoyance for the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 across is HAYMAKERS, which begins with H; the definition is the name of that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter H is spelt out in words as this, and H opens the answer to 23 across.

clue.text: Teacher's expression of disapproval — nothing right!

parts.note: tut is the noise of disapproval
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A teacher tuts at a pupil who got nothing right.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher or a university instructor.

clue.text: Punches for some working in the sunshine?

explanation.surface: Blows thrown by those labouring outdoors in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: These are wild swinging punches in boxing, and also farmhands who cut and dry hay in fine weather.

clue.text: One of the flight included in case?

definitions.text: One of the flight included in case?

parts.words: One of the flight included in case?
parts.note: one step of a flight, put in front of the word case

explanation.surface: A question about whether a member of the squadron went into the box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests aircraft or birds, but it is a set of steps; 'case' completes the compound for the whole stairwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step in a staircase, one of a flight.

clue.text: Recited in pub to a leading journalist

indicators.note: the word to goes in, placed inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
ED is short for editor, the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: Someone speaks in a bar to a top newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to recite or chant in a measured, level voice.

clue.text: First-class: beer in return for a big cigar

indicators.note: in return means coming back, so the whole sequence is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, here as the letters AI
lager is a beer

explanation.surface: A top-quality beer swapped for a large cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written as AI; AILAGER read backwards is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A regalia is a large, high-quality cigar, a sense quite apart from royal emblems.

clue.text: Sweet-and-sour? It may be

explanation.surface: A question about a dish with a sweet-and-sour flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart is a pastry dessert, a sweet; and tart as an adjective means sharp or acid in taste.

clue.text: Having no partner, one grows wild

explanation.surface: Someone without a partner who goes off the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: At a dance, a person left without a partner is called this; it is also a fragrant plant that grows wild on old walls.
